title: Analyzing and Improving Fine-grained Preference Optimization in Medical LVLMs
abstract: arXiv:2606.12590v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Preference optimization is increasingly used to post-train medical large vision-language models (LVLMs), yet it operates at a much coarser granularity than the one that defines clinical correctness. Whether one response is clinically better than another usually comes down to a few decisive phrases, such as an anatomical laterality or a lesion attribute, and to whether each is supported by the image region the question concerns. Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and its variants, by contrast, reduce the comparison to a single response-level scalar, an objective structurally unable to represent which tokens carry clinical meaning. translated_title: 分析与改进医学大型视觉语言模型中的细粒度偏好优化
translated_abstract: 偏好优化越来越多地被用于医学大型视觉语言模型（LVLMs）的后训练，然而其运作的粒度远比定义临床正确性的粒度粗糙。判断一个回答是否在临床上优于另一个回答，通常取决于少数几个决定性的短语，例如解剖学方位（左右侧）或病灶属性，以及这些短语是否得到问题所涉及的图像区域的支持。相比之下，直接偏好优化（DPO）及其变体将这种比较简化为单一的回答级别标量，这种目标在结构上无法表示哪些词元承载着临床意义。我们证明这种不匹配代价高昂：在我们比较的各项目标中，回答级别的DPO对决定临床正确性的短语给予的奖励最少；而用监督参考答案替代偏好回答则会打开一个风格上的差距，模型会将这一差距作为奖励作弊的捷径加以利用……
tldr: 该论文指出医学LVLMs中回答级别的DPO偏好优化粒度过粗，无法奖励决定临床正确性的关键短语（如解剖方位、病灶属性）并导致奖励作弊等问题，据此提出细粒度（词元级别）的偏好优化方法以提升模型临床回答的可靠性。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that response-level DPO is too coarse for medical LVLMs—failing to reward the few decisive phrases that determine clinical correctness and enabling reward-hacking via stylistic shortcuts—and proposes a fine-grained, token-level preference optimization approach to address this.
